Validate an adjustment set

Source: R/identification.R
is_valid_adjustment.Rd

Tests the Generalized Adjustment Criterion, which covers DAGs, ADMGs, PDAG-family graphs, MAG-family graphs, and PAGs alike: given must contain no forbidden node (a descendant of a proper causal node between x and y, or x itself), and must m-separate x from y in the proper backdoor graph.

Usage

is_valid_adjustment(cg, x, y, given = character())

Arguments

cg

A DAG, ADMG, PDAG-family (PDAG, CPDAG, MPDAG), AG-family (AG, MAG), or PAG graph created with cgraph().

x, y

Exposure and outcome node name, or character vector of node names.

given

Character vector of adjustment node names (may be empty).

Value

TRUE if given satisfies the adjustment criterion for identifying the causal effect of x on y.

References

Perković E, Textor J, Kalisch M, Maathuis MH (2018). “Complete Graphical Characterization and Construction of Adjustment Sets in Markov Equivalence Classes of Ancestral Graphs.” Journal of Machine Learning Research, 18, 1–62.

Examples

if (julia_ready()) {
  admg <- cgraph(L %-->% X, X %-->% Y, L %-->% Y, class = "ADMG")
  list(
    empty = is_valid_adjustment(admg, "X", "Y"), # L --> Y not blocked
    conditioned_on_l = is_valid_adjustment(admg, "X", "Y", "L")
  )
}
#> $empty
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $conditioned_on_l
#> [1] TRUE
#>
